title: Private/VPC residency policy and audit evidence pipeline for constrained regional failover
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Problem: Customers running Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) require strict controls over where their data may reside, how long it is retained, and machine-readable evidence that residency/retention policies were honored during normal operation and failover. Current Private control plane allows region preference but lacks tenant-level enforced residency constraints, retention enforcement hooks, and an automated evidence/reporting pipeline that produces cryptographically-signed compliance bundles for audits.

Goal: Build a tenant-configurable residency policy and retention settings module for Private deployments that: (1) enforces residency constraints at the request-routing and replication layer, (2) provides per-tenant retention lifecycle controls with enforcement in storage/kv-cache layers, and (3) produces automated compliance evidence (signed logs + config snapshots + metric proofs) when failover or replication events occur. Include controls to restrict automatic cross-region failover unless a tenant opts in via an auditable policy and explicit SLA waiver.

Scope: Private/VPC and on-prem control plane changes only (customer-managed control plane option). Hosted API and Dedicated will be out-of-scope for initial implementation but design should be portable. This ticket covers schema, enforcement hooks in routing/orchestrator, retention enforcement points, evidence bundle format, KMS signing integration, and a minimal UI/CLI for operators to view and export evidence bundles.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant residency policy schema supports allow-list of regions, disallowed regions, and a 'no-automatic-failover' flag
Routing layer checks tenant policy before promoting replica or redirecting traffic; attempt to cross-region without explicit opt-in is blocked and logged
Retention settings (per-tenant) configurable: retention_days, retention_policy (delete|archive|quarantine) and enforced in KV-cache and persistent store

Automated evidence bundle generated on any failover/replication event containing: policy snapshot, routing decision log, storage retention actions, and metric summary; bundle is signed with customer or Redwood KMS key
Admin UI / CLI command exists to export evidence bundle for a given tenant and timeframe
E2E test demonstrating: tenant with 'no-automatic-failover' flagged in region A is not moved to region B during simulated capacity pressure
Security review completed and KMS integration approved by Security team
Performance regression <5% p99 request latency in greenfield Private clusters after adding residency checks (measured in canary)
comments: 2025-01-16 - Kickoff: meeting with Product (Aisha Patel), Security (Ethan Brooks), and Infra SRE (Lena Varga). Agreed to require explicit tenant opt-in for cross-region failover. Action: produce schema and enforcement plan.

2025-01-22 - Initial schema draft posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIV/Residency+Policy+Spec . Feedback: include 'business_justification' free-text field to record audit rationale when customer opts into failover.

2025-01-29 - Prototype routing check implemented in orchestrator (branch: feat/residency-checks). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1893 . Basic tests pass; needs KMS signing and retention hook integration.
2025-02-03 - Security review session: agreed to support both customer key-signing and Redwood-signed bundles. Added HSM/KMS rotation notes to spec.

2025-02-07 - SRE: simulated failover run with synthetic load. Observed retention deletion lag in one on-prem store; created follow-up ENG-9451 to surface retention enforcement metrics and blocking behavior.
2025-02-10 - Product review: Priya approved scope for MVP evidence bundle format. Next: implement UI export endpoint and wire KMS signing path.
decisions: Use tenant-level JSON policy stored in control-plane database; policy validated on write and cached on the dataplane nodes for fast checks
Enforcement point: Routing/orchestrator will make final decision and emit signed decision event; storage layers must respect retention TTLs enforced by control plane job
Evidence bundle format: tar.gz with JSON manifests, routing logs (NDJSON), storage action manifest, and a signed SHA256 checksum file; customers may provide public key for signature verification
Cross-region failover default: allowed=false; only changed via API with 'business_justification' and recorded in audit trail
KMS: support both customer-managed KMS keys (recommended) and Redwood-escrowed keys for customers without KMS; all keys must be registered and approved by Security
